## ✨ Added

- Seekable encryption format (`cf=2`): a new per-file content format where each 64 KiB chunk is encrypted on its own with XChaCha20-Poly1305, so any chunk can be decrypted independently. That gives large encrypted videos real random-access seeking: the preview fetches and decrypts only the chunks it needs instead of starting from the beginning. New uploads use the seekable format automatically, and existing shares in the sequential format keep working unchanged. It is still zero-knowledge, and the security core had an independent review.

## 🎨 Design

- A redesigned home page in a clean, Smash-style layout. There's no separate drop-zone box anymore: the big, responsive, centered logo is the upload target. Click it to pick files, or drag files anywhere onto the page. The text moves to the top.
- The "Your link is ready" window has a cleaner layout (share link and QR), and the two copy buttons now share one colour.
- A bigger inline preview: images, videos and PDFs render at a proper viewing size instead of a small thumbnail. The extra icon inside the download card is gone, since the brand header already carries it.
- Centered windows everywhere: the feather, the options panel, the result card and the download page all sit in the middle of the viewport. Choosing a file cross-fades the feather into the options panel, with the upload progress below it, and the copy-link button has a clear hover state.
- A new banner claim, "Big files, zero baggage.", and copy that presents featherdrop as your own private, self-hosted WeTransfer (no accounts, no size paywalls, links that self-destruct on schedule) in the README, the GitHub repo description and the Unraid template and CA feed card. `.github/assets/gen-banner.mjs` regenerates the banner SVG and PNG. The feather and wordmark stay as they are, and only the claim is redrawn, set in Lato.
- Browser-tab favicon: the transparent gold gradient feather (`public/favicon.svg`) is linked from the app shell and served at `/favicon.svg` as `image/svg+xml`.
- Startup log banner: on boot the server prints the shared "Junker der Provinz" ASCII banner and a big `FEATHERDROP IS READY` box to stdout, like the other own-image containers, so you can spot a running instance in the Docker or Unraid log at a glance.

## ⚡ Improved

- The server is a single static Go binary: the same app, the same zero-knowledge guarantees and the same features, but a tiny image with no Node runtime. The browser-side crypto and the whole UI stay in TypeScript. Only the server moved.
- One CGO-free Go binary (`chi`, `tusd` and the pure-Go `modernc.org/sqlite`) replaces the Node and Next.js server. It serves the React client as embedded static assets along with the JSON and file API. The result is a ~15 MB `distroless` image, much lower RAM use, proper HTTP streaming and Range support, and no more trouble building native addons.
- A drop-in upgrade: the SQLite schema matches the old one byte for byte and the blob layout is unchanged, so the server opens the same `db.sqlite` and the same `/config` and `/data` volumes and serves existing shares exactly as before. Ports, environment variables and volumes stay the same, so your `docker run` doesn't change. If you ever need to roll back, the previous Node image is still buildable from `Dockerfile.next`.
- Uploads go in 64 MiB chunks, so they get through size-capped proxies and really resume. A CDN with a request-body limit (Cloudflare Free and Pro cap it at 100 MB) answers a single large PATCH request with 413. Chunked uploads of any size pass through Cloudflare, and an interrupted upload resumes from the last chunk instead of starting over.
- Every auth gate (the upload password and the download key verifier) is enforced on the server and in constant time. A full adversarial security audit found no blocking issues. CI builds and boots the image and runs the real zero-knowledge browser round trip (upload, download, preview, multi-file) against the Go server on every change, and runs `govulncheck` on the dependencies.
- The key verifier covers the seekable format too. For `cf=2` shares the uploader's browser stores a one-way verifier (`base64url(SHA-256(content key))`, in a nullable `key_verifier` column), and `GET /api/d/<slug>` must present the same value in the `x-fd-key-verifier` header, compared in constant time, before anything is counted or served. A missing or wrong verifier gets a 401 with no side effects, so someone who only learned the slug from a proxy or access log can't use up a limited share and destroy the file. The verifier reveals nothing about the key, and the server still can't decrypt. The client derives the key before fetching, so a wrong password fails without a request, and both download paths (the button and the small-file preview prefetch) send the header. Shares without a stored verifier (`key_verifier` NULL) keep downloading as before.
- More formats for the inline video preview: `.mkv`, `.avi`, `.mpeg`, `.3gp`, `.wmv`, `.flv`, `.ts` and more. A preview only plays when the browser can decode the codec inside the container. MP4, WebM, OGG and MOV are reliable. AVI, WMV and FLV usually aren't, and they show a safe, inert player.
- Faster to start: the streamed preview serves a bounded window per request instead of fetching and decrypting the whole file up front, so playback begins quickly instead of hanging on a long first load.
- The management link is gone: shares are removed by their expiry, and by the download limit if you set one. That's simpler and one less secret to keep. Management links that were already handed out stop working.
- Reverse-proxy docs (README §8) explain that a proxying CDN enforces its own request-body limit before your reverse proxy sees the request, so `client_max_body_size 0` can't override Cloudflare's 100 MB. The 64 MiB upload chunks get through either way. There's also a short comparison of the remote-access options: direct or port-forward, Cloudflare Tunnel, or a self-hosted tunnel (for example Pangolin on a small VPS).
- The Go toolchain is pinned to `go1.26.5`, which carries the standard-library fix for GO-2026-5856 (an Encrypted Client Hello privacy leak in `crypto/tls`).

## 🐛 Fixed

- The inline preview of large videos (over the in-memory cap and streamed through the service worker) now works on the first visit to a share link, not only after a manual reload. The streaming preview used to give up before the service worker had taken control of the page, so no preview appeared.
